# ADR 0029 amendment: the perspective-selection contract, before its leaves

Leaf of #18605 (parent linked natively) — **the first leaf by the record's own rule.** `Decision Record: Required: ADR 0029 amend` · `Decision Record impact: amends ADR 0029`.

## Context

D#18594 graduated with Vega's STEP_BACK verdict (`DC_kwDODSospM4BGPHO`, acknowledged per row in the author's comment 6): ADR 0029 is **amended**, not challenged, and the amendment carries four obligations, (a)–(d) below. `learn/agentos/decisions/0029-docking-design.md:765` — *"a leaf that contradicts a section here amends this ADR first, in its own reviewed change (ADR-0005 lifecycle)"* — is why this leaf merges before any other leaf of the epic opens as ready.

## The Problem

Three sentences in the record will be retrieved by future sessions as authority, and each contradicts the graduated shape:

- `:68–69` (§2.1, stage one): *"This tier is initial-only: reactive declaration reconciliation, perspective/storage configuration and multi-workspace authoring are separate contracts."* — the epic puts a reactive selection on the host. A note beside the sentence cannot re-mean it; a retrieval returns the sentence.
- `:117` (§2.1): *"Every future docking leaf classifies each new piece of state into exactly one row of this table before implementation."* — the epic introduces three pieces of state (the accepted intent, the committed name, the pending request) and none has a row.
- `:211–212` (§2.2): *"`layoutId` is the topology identity; a collection's `activeLayoutId` must name one entry in its `topologies` record."* — consumers read this as selection (the Workstation controller reads `activeLayoutId` by hand at `apps/workstation/view/WorkspaceController.mjs:53`), while under auto-save (`persistence/TopologyLibrary.mjs:114–116` → `:155`, `replace: true`) the pointer is rewritten on every commit and means nothing about what the user chose.

The §5 decomposition table (`:721`) lists the leaves the record gates; the epic has no row.

## The Architectural Reality

`Neo.tab.Container#activeIndex_` (`src/tab/Container.mjs:56–59`), `layout.Card#activeIndex_` (`src/layout/Card.mjs:49–51`) and `toolbar.Breadcrumb#activeKey_` (`src/toolbar/Breadcrumb.mjs:23–26`) are the idiom the record now admits for the Workspace: a reactive intent config, a committed truth published beside it, an event. The state classes the record's §2.1 table already distinguishes (component-owned reactive config · worker-owned shared truth · transient request state) are exactly the three rows the epic needs.

## The Fix

Documentation-only PR against `learn/agentos/decisions/0029-docking-design.md` plus two JSDoc mirrors:

- **(a)** rewrite `:68–69` **in place**; quote the former sentence verbatim in the same paragraph as provenance ("stage one read: …"); the successor sentence names the selection contract as stage two and keeps the bound-catalog tier and multi-workspace authoring as still-separate contracts.
- **(b)** add exactly one row each to the §2.1 state-class table: `activePerspective_` — accepted intent, component-owned reactive config; the committed perspective name — accepted-write identity, carried in the write's descriptor `{workspaceKey, before, after}`, published as `dock.perspective.active`; `dock.perspective.pending` — request-lifecycle state under the request serial. State that wants two rows is two pieces of state (`:117`).
- **(c)** restate `:211–212` as a collection invariant with no selection meaning ("names one entry; it is a consumer-owned pointer, never the selected perspective"), and mirror the sentence in the `activeLayoutId` docblocks of `src/dashboard/dock/persistence/PerspectiveLibrary.mjs` and `src/dashboard/dock/persistence/TopologyLibrary.mjs` (JSDoc lines only).
- **(d)** add the epic's row to the §5 decomposition table: leaf #18605, contract sections §2.1 + §2.2, status "graduated from D#18594".
- §2.2 gains the selection contract in four sentences: the declared list is the only name source at this stage; a saved record is a snapshot that may equal but never define a perspective; the reserved name for the unnamed declared perspective is refused at both persisted write boundaries; origin metadata follows the accepted-write identity, never the published leaf.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `:68–69` rewritten in place; the former sentence quoted verbatim as provenance in the same paragraph; no "note" or "see also" substitute.
- [ ] The §2.1 state-class table has one row each for `activePerspective_`, the committed perspective name and `dock.perspective.pending`, with the class named per row; a reviewer can place every piece of state the epic's engine leaves introduce into exactly one of them.
- [ ] `:211–212` states `activeLayoutId` as a collection invariant without selection meaning; the two persistence docblocks carry the mirrored sentence; no runtime line changes.
- [ ] §2.2 carries the four-sentence selection contract; §5's decomposition table has the epic's row.
- [ ] The PR touches only the ADR and the two docblocks, and merges before any other #18605 leaf's PR leaves draft (the `:765` rule); the epic's other leaves are `blocked_by` this one natively.
- [ ] Cross-family review from the GPT family (the author's family cannot clear its own graduation's first leaf).

## Out of Scope

Any engine, example, app or guide change (own leaves). The bound-catalog tier and saved-name selection (deferred with triggers in #18605).

## Avoided Traps

A footnote or "amendment" section that leaves `:68–69` intact (retrieval returns the old sentence); a fifth state class instead of the three existing rows; converting `activeLayoutId` into the selection (the Workstation's auto-save rewrites it on every commit).
